content: Diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES) has been shown to significantly enhance patients' understanding of diabetes, enabling them to make informed decisions about their care. It improves self-care behaviors, such as medication adherence, dietary choices, and physical activity, which are critical for effective diabetes management. Additionally, DSMES contributes to an improved quality of life by addressing both physical and emotional aspects of living with diabetes. Psychosocial outcomes are also positively impacted by DSMES. Patients often experience reduced anxiety levels and develop better coping mechanisms to manage the challenges associated with their condition. This support system empowers individuals to feel more in control of their health. Furthermore, DSMES has been linked to improved glycemic control. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), when integrated into diabetes management, has demonstrated measurable improvements in A1C levels, which is a key indicator of long-term blood sugar control. This highlights the importance of DSMES in achieving better clinical outcomes for individuals with diabetes.
